doc.title: Last Straws: John Chaffe, Bris Jones, Bill Lee, Frank De La Houssaye, Bob Ice Interview, 1960-04-18

title: Music around Woodville and Lee's first jazz group
summary: After talk of Natchez and Woodville, Lee says there was no jazz there, only pop. He played hillbilly bands and led his own small jazz group about eight years earlier.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I've been through there. I was selling fish there, I noticed, last weekend. I was at, right on the square. I was looking for a guitar player from there, Scott Dunbar. Oh? Yeah, he's a real good guitar player. He's made some records. When were you there? A couple of weeks ago, I was on my way to Natchez.
Well, I was in Natchez two weeks ago. In fact, I went to Woodville the same weekend, I bet you. Were you there on a Sunday?

I was there, I guess, on a Saturday, I think I got there. Oh, no. Went on up to Natchez. I just missed you. That's funny. Did you hear any bands around there that were playing any jazz when you were growing up?
No. No, not around my part of the country. Not at all. What did they play? How's that?
What did they play up there? What kind of music?
Well, you had a band on Saturday nights and such on the weekends, but it wasn't necessarily jazz. In fact, it never was jazz. Just regular pop.
No. No, I never recall any hillbilly from that part of the country.
Did you play with dance bands then?

No, I didn't. I never played in Woodville. Well, yeah, I did. I had a little band there myself, but otherwise I never played with anybody else there. But I have played with hillbilly bands, and that was mostly over around Bristol's country. Incidentally, around Bogalusa. And, of course, down here.
When did you start playing jazz? I've been trying ever since I've... Ever since you started. But, I mean, when did you first play with a jazz band?
Well, I had a little group of my own about eight years ago, I guess. Roughly eight years ago. And we called ourselves jazz players. And then the last straws, I guess that's about all. That's it.
